T: Change your fate. Not the cake.
D: A Scottish princess's wish to change her fate turns her mother into a bear.
P: Serve dessert when Merida feeds her mum the witch's cake.
S: Jammy soft-boiled eggs wrapped in sage and pepper sausage meat, crumbed and fried until golden, halved and served with wholegrain mustard. Boil 6 eggs for 6 minutes, cool and peel. Mix 500g sausage meat with sage and pepper, wrap around each egg, roll in flour, beaten egg and breadcrumbs and fry at 170C for 8 minutes. Halve and serve with mustard.
Elinor as a bear learning to catch fish in the river
Oatcakes spread with cream cheese, topped with folds of smoked salmon, dill and a squeeze of lemon, laid out on a slate.
Merida's little brothers pinching the tarts

Shortcrust rounds pressed into a patty tin, filled with raspberry jam, baked at 190C for 15 minutes and dusted with icing sugar. Roll 2 sheets shortcrust pastry to 3mm and cut 12 rounds with an 8cm cutter. Press into a greased patty tin and prick the bases. Spoon 1 heaped teaspoon of raspberry jam into each, no more or it will bubble over. Bake at 190C for 15 minutes until the pastry is golden. Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, as the jam is very hot, then lift out and dust with icing sugar. Serve with whipped cream.
M: DunBroch braised lamb, neeps and tatties
the great hall feast at DunBroch

Lamb shoulder braised 3 hours with onion, carrots, barley and stock, served with mashed neeps and tatties. Season 1.5kg lamb shoulder and brown all over in a heavy pot. Add 2 chopped onions, 3 chunky carrots, 75g pearl barley, 2 rosemary sprigs and 750ml chicken stock. Cover and braise at 160C for 3 hours until it pulls apart. Boil 800g peeled potatoes and 600g swede separately until soft. Mash the potatoes with 50g butter and milk, and the swede with 30g butter and pepper. Serve the lamb and barley over both mashes with the juices.
Lamb neck simmered with barley, leek, carrot and turnip for 2 hours, finished with parsley.
W: the cake from the witch that changes Elinor
A spiced honey cake with oats and berries, baked at 175C for 40 minutes, glazed with honey and topped with a raspberry.
K: Raspberries blended with milk, honey and toasted oats, poured into tall glasses with cream on top.

s.how: Boil 6 eggs for 6 minutes, cool and peel. Mix 500g sausage meat with sage and pepper, wrap around each egg, roll in flour, beaten egg and breadcrumbs and fry at 170C for 8 minutes. Halve and serve with mustard.

s.note: Elinor as a bear learning to catch fish in the river
s.how: Spread oatcakes with cream cheese. Top with folds of smoked salmon and a sprig of dill. Squeeze over a little lemon and lay them out on a slate. Any bears in the house will want the lot.

m.how: Simmer 1kg lamb neck with 150g pearl barley in 2L water for an hour. Add 2 sliced leeks, 3 diced carrots and 2 diced turnips and simmer another hour. Shred the lamb back in, season well and stir through chopped parsley.

w.note: the cake from the witch that changes Elinor
w.how: Beat 125g butter with 150g honey, then 2 eggs. Fold in 200g self-raising flour, 50g rolled oats and a handful of raspberries. Bake at 175C for 40 minutes. Glaze with warm honey and set a single raspberry on top. Do not feed it to your mum.

d.how: Toast 2 tbsp rolled oats in a dry pan until golden. Blend 200g raspberries with 750ml cold milk, 2 tbsp honey and most of the oats until smooth. Pour into tall glasses, top with whipped cream and the rest of the oats.
